name: SpaceX Starship V3 (Super Heavy 33×Raptor 3 + Ship 3 SL + 3 RVac Raptor 3) — TIMELINE mode

diameter_m.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Super Heavy diameter 9 m / 29.5 ft

propellant_kg.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Super Heavy propellant capacity 3,650 t / 8 Mlb

dry_kg.assumption: Super Heavy V3 empty mass is still unpublished on the SpaceX specs page. 275 t is the earlier-block empty mass on the Wikipedia Super Heavy infobox (gross 3,675 t with 3,400 t propellant). Labelled stand-in, NOT a V3 measurement.

thrust_sl_N.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Super Heavy thrust 8,240 tf / 18.1 Mlbf (8,240 × 1,000 × 9.80665 = 80,806,796 N). Equals 33 × ~249.7 tf, matching the 250 tf Raptor 3 sea-level rating on the same page and the 12 May 2026 V3 update.

thrust_vac_N.derived: 33 × 263.00 tf, the per-engine vacuum thrust implied by the official Ship 1,614 tf total minus 3 × 275 tf RVac (see ship stage). Same Raptor 3 sea-level engines as the ship. 85,111,915 N.

isp_vac_s.note: Elon Musk, 9 Sep 2019: 'Sea level Raptor’s vacuum Isp is ~350 sec, but ~380 sec with larger vacuum-optimized nozzle.' SpaceX's 3 Aug 2024 Raptor 3 (sea-level variant) post also listed 350 s. Used as vacuum Isp for the 33 sea-level Raptor 3s.

cutoff_s.note: SpaceX F15 post-launch timeline: Super Heavy MECO (most engines cut off) T+00:02:19

separation_s.note: SpaceX F15: Hot-staging (Starship Raptor ignition and stage separation) T+00:02:21. Unburned Super Heavy residual stands in for the unpublished boostback/landing reserve (boostback T+2:26–3:02, landing burn T+6:10–6:35 and catch, not modelled). F14 official narrative: boostback used 31 of 33 engines; that reserve stays on the booster and is not delivered to the ship.

diameter_m.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Starship diameter 9 m / 29.5 ft

propellant_kg.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Starship propellant capacity 1,600 t / 3.5 Mlb. Not increased above this figure.

dry_kg.assumption: Starship V3 dry mass unpublished. Elon Musk in 2021 quoted ~100 t for a much earlier ship. 120 t is a labelled stand-in for a V3 ship, NOT a measurement.

thrust_vac_N.note: SpaceX technical specifications: Ship thrust 1,614 tf (15,827,933 N). That is the official rated/initial thrust of 3 sea-level + 3 RVac Raptor 3s (3×263.00 tf vac implied + 3×275 tf = 1,614 tf). Held for the published 348 s ascent. At blended Isp 364.72 s this burns 1,540 t of the 1,600 t load and leaves 60 t residual — enough to fly the published 20 s insertion (14.3 t at 250 tf / 350 s) with propellant left for the unmodelled deorbit/catch. A deeper 80.7% mean ascent throttle, tried in order to make a full-thrust 20 s / 250 tf insertion only 94 m/s, left too little Δv to reach the passively safe ellipse. Ascent is therefore flown at the official 1,614 tf; the insertion burn is throttled instead (see launch post_cutoff).

thrust_sl_N.assumption: Hot-stage start is already ~60–80 km (above essentially all atmosphere); official 1,614 tf vacuum/rated thrust is used. Sea-level stack would be 3×250 tf plus three RVacs not rated for SL.

isp_vac_s.derived: Blended vacuum Isp of 3 sea-level Raptor 3s at 350 s and 3 RVacs at 380 s, mass-flow weighted at the official 1,614 tf / 275 tf split: mdot_full = 3×2,579,149/(350×g0) + 3×2,696,829/(380×g0) = 4,425.34 kg/s; Isp = 15,827,933/(mdot×g0) = 364.72 s. 350 s / 380 s from Musk 9 Sep 2019 (sea-level Raptor vacuum Isp ~350 s, ~380 s with the larger vacuum-optimized nozzle). The previous model used a single 350 s for all six engines and over-burned the tank.

ignition_s.note: F15 hot-staging / Starship Raptor ignition T+00:02:21. F14 official narrative: ship ignites all six Raptor engines (3 sea-level + 3 vacuum) on ascent.

cutoff_s.note: F15 Starship engine cutoff T+00:08:09 (ascent burn). Orbital insertion burn is a later restart (T+26:10–26:30) and is modelled in post_cutoff, not in this cutoff.

mass_kg.assumption: no jettisoned payload fairing; Starlink V3 stack is carried internally and deployed through a door. Mass 0 so the jettison event is a no-op.

jettison_time_s.assumption: dummy time at staging; fairing mass is 0

cd.assumption: not published; generic Cd. A 9 m cylinder would have a different (unpublished) coefficient; not fitted.

payload_kg.basis: 26 Starlink V3 satellites, mass unpublished by SpaceX. Fitted payload is a steering parameter, NOT an estimate of the real stack.

header_notes: Starship V3 from SpaceX technical specifications (https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/starship/technical-specifications): Super Heavy 3,650 t propellant, 8,240 tf / 18.1 Mlbf, 9 m; Ship 1,600 t propellant, 1,614 tf, 9 m. Raptor 3 sea-level 250 tf (same page and SpaceX 'Introducing Starship V3' update, 12 May 2026, https://www.spacex.com/updates/starship-v3). RVac 275 tf (same 12 May 2026 update, up from 258 tf). Engine counts: 33 Raptor 3 on Super Heavy; Ship 3 sea-level + 3 RVac (SpaceX specs page; F14 official narrative: all six on ascent).

Previous file used 1,600 tf (rounded Wikipedia 'initial thrust') and a single 350 s Isp for all six ship engines, held constant for 348 s, which left only 9.1 t residual and could not fly the published 20 s insertion. Units were already correct (1,600/1,614 tf is the ship, Super Heavy is 8,240 tf). This revision uses official 1,614 tf and blended 364.72 s Isp; residual after ascent is ~60 t. Insertion is the published 20 s burn with thrust solved to a 275 km perigee (labelled Raptor throttle), not a residual-limited 12.8 s at 250 tf.

TIMELINE mode uses SpaceX's published Flight 15 event times (content.spacex.com/api/spacex-website/missions/starship-flight-15): MECO 139 s, hot-stage / ship ignition 141 s, ship ascent cutoff 489 s. Boostback and catch are not modelled; unburned booster propellant stands in for the recovery reserve and is not delivered to the ship.

The 20 s orbital insertion burn (T+26:10–26:30) and payload deploy (start 35:01, complete 1:17:40) are flown in post_cutoff. SpaceX F15: ~275 km, ~14 orbits, >22-hour flight, with a passively safe suborbital opportunity before raising to orbital altitude (same architecture as F14). F14 official: single sea-level Raptor insertion after a passively safe suborbital trajectory.
